stop_reason: Max iterations (2) reached. The primary CDC FluView Week 40 2024 source is confirmed in the result set. State-level sources (Mississippi, New York, Florida, Illinois, Wisconsin) and international/news sources appeared in iteration 2 results. No additional search iterations are possible or warranted.
final_coverage_assessment: Core coverage is adequate for the task window. The CDC FluView Week 40 2024 report (ending Oct 5, 2024) is the definitive national-level source and was confirmed in iteration 1. The Mississippi MSDH PDF explicitly covers Sept. 29–Oct. 5, 2024 with ILI rate data. Iteration 2 surfaced additional state-level domains (health.ny.gov, floridahealth.gov, dph.illinois.gov, slh.wisc.edu) and PAHO results (×4), plus news sources (Reuters, NBC, ABC, CIDRAP). The FluSurv-NET overview page was retrieved but is a methodology page, not a week-specific data page — week 40 hospitalization rates would need to be extracted from FluView Interactive. The WHO result retrieved (cdn.who.int update #466) is dated March 2024, not October 2024, so it does not cover the task window; however, PAHO results (×4) may include relevant October 2024 regional bulletins. Overall, national and subnational coverage is sufficient for the target fields given the early-season, low-activity nature of Week 40 2024.
final_trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources dominate: CDC FluView (cdc.gov) is the gold standard for U.S. influenza surveillance. MSDH (msdh.ms.gov) is an official state .gov source with explicit week 40 2024 date range. PAHO (paho.org) is an authoritative international organization. State .gov domains (health.ny.gov, floridahealth.gov, dph.illinois.gov) are official. CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a reputable academic public health news source. Reuters and NBC/ABC are credible mainstream news outlets. The WHO cdn.who.int result is a March 2024 update (wrong time window) and should not be used as evidence for October 2024. The Facebook/AAP post and familiesfightingflu.org are season-level, not week-specific, and should be treated as secondary corroboration only. The nnph.org Week 10 2024-2025 PDF covers a different week (Week 10, not Week 40) and should not be used for the task window.
